issue.title: Add a --version flag to the CLI
issue.body:
Running `todo --version` currently prints an error. It should print the installed version, for example `todo-cli 0.3.1`.

The version number already lives in `todo/__init__.py` as `__version__`.

comments.author: maintainer-jo
comments.body: Good first issue! argparse has a built-in 'version' action that does most of the work.

repo_info.description: A tiny command line to-do list manager

explanation.simple_explanation: The command line tool has no way to tell you which version is installed. Typing `todo --version` should print the version number, but right now it shows an error. The version number is already stored in the code, so you only need to connect it to the command.
explanation.what_success_looks_like: Running `todo --version` prints `todo-cli 0.3.1` (using the real version) and exits without an error.

pr_draft.title: Add --version flag to the CLI
pr_draft.description:
## What I changed
- Added a `--version` option in `todo/cli.py` that prints the value of `__version__`.
- Added a test in `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Why
Users had no way to check which version of todo-cli is installed.

## How I tested
- Ran `pytest` and all tests pass.
- Ran `todo --version` and saw `todo-cli 0.3.1`.

Closes #42
